hypotheses.justification: hA follows from hfa: take i = 0, which satisfies 0 ≤ m for any m : ℕ. Then 0 ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ ≤ A, so A ≥ 0. To prove the theorem without hA, add `have hA : 0 ≤ A := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hfa 0 (Nat.zero_le m))` and leave the rest of the proof unchanged. hB can be removed in the same way, so deleting both together also works.

hB follows from hgb: take i = 0, which satisfies 0 ≤ m for any m : ℕ. Then 0 ≤ ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 g x‖ ≤ B, so B ≥ 0. To prove the theorem without hB, add `have hB : 0 ≤ B := (norm_nonneg _).trans (hgb 0 (Nat.zero_le m))` and leave the rest of the proof unchanged. This does not depend on whether hA is kept, so deleting both together also works.
